about: GLM-5.3-Flash, Mia TensorFold EXL3 4 bpw checkpoint with a DFlash2 drafter, on TensorFold v0.6.0 plus the repository's patches (0109: sixteen decode streams), tensor-parallel over four DGX Sparks on RoCE: 16 requests at once, a 1,048,576-token window (MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold, TP=4 branch)
setup: Four DGX Sparks on one RoCE switch (ConnectX-7, every pair on a shared subnet, the same MTU everywhere), one rank each; rank 0 drives the others over key-based ssh and serves the API on 8888. One-command route: clone the source at the commit below on the head, copy scripts/local.sh.example to scripts/local.sh and set WORKER, WORKER2 and WORKER3 (ssh targets of ranks 1 to 3), MASTER_ADDR (an address of the head that every worker reaches) and SOCKET_NET (the address prefix of the network all four share, which picks each node's NCCL bootstrap netdev), then run ./start-tp4.sh: the first start builds the image from the repository's patches (TensorFold v0.6.0 plus patches/*.patch, 0109 sixteen streams included; the same steps as its Dockerfile), downloads the two pinned weights (~164 GiB) and copies image and weights to the workers, compiles kernels, starts ranks 3 to 0 and waits for the API (about 5 minutes once the image and weights are there). By hand: build the image with the Dockerfile, put both pinned repositories in ~/.cache/huggingface on every node, and run the container on each node with NODE_RANK 0 to 3, HEAD_IP = rank 0's address on the link every rank reaches, CX7_IF = the netdev of the shared network (NCCL bootstrap), CX7_IB = that node's RoCE devices as a comma list (both PCIe twins of the cabled port), GID_INDEX = the RoCE v2 GID index holding its IPv4 address, KERNEL_CACHE = a host directory for compiled kernels. Memory: each Spark needs ~110 GiB free at start; with a ~1M-token prompt in flight at least 10 GiB must stay free on every node (measured: 14.5 GiB lowest, rank 0, a 997k-token prompt with 15 other streams decoding).
